_comment: Scripted FakeLlmProvider output for a tailor run against resume/sample-1.pdf (Priya Raghavan — Convoy/Zulily), which is the résumé the phase-8 golden path imports. It exists because tailor-stripe.json was recorded against alex-chen: its citations address paths that do not exist in Priya's document, so every proposal was refused and the golden path saw no diff-row at all. That refusal was CORRECT — the guard was doing its job on a fixture aimed at the wrong résumé — but it left the end-to-end script unable to reach the review UI it exists to prove. Guarded by "Convoy", which appears in Priya's résumé JSON inside the prompt and in no other fixture's; tailor-stripe.json stays the unguarded default, so alex-chen runs are untouched. The three entries are deliberately one of each outcome the review screen has to render: a cited edit that must survive validation (its snippet is byte-identical to expected-1.json), an uncited add that must be REFUSED and shown struck through, and a second cited edit so the accept-all path has more than one row to apply. Do not 'fix' the refusal — a fixture where everything passes would stop testing the thing that makes this product different.
response: {"changes": [{"kind": "edit", "path": "experience[0].bullets[0]", "now": "Rebuilt the freight pricing feature store on Iceberg, cutting model training time from 6 hours to 40 minutes — the batch-to-serving latency work this role leads with", "why": "The posting opens on pipeline latency and model serving; the original bullet has the number but buries what it was in service of.", "citation": {"path": "experience[0].bullets[0]", "snippet": "Rebuilt the freight pricing feature store on Iceberg, cutting model training time from 6 hours to 40 minutes"}}, {"kind": "add", "path": "experience[0].bullets", "now": "Led a 9-person platform team through a company-wide migration to exactly-once payment processing", "why": "The JD asks for leadership at scale and payments exposure.", "citation": null}, {"kind": "edit", "path": "experience[1].bullets[0]", "now": "Migrated 200 nightly Hive jobs to Spark on Kubernetes, halving warehouse spend — the cost-per-query discipline the posting asks for", "why": "The posting names infrastructure cost explicitly; this is the one bullet that already carries a spend number.", "citation": {"path": "experience[1].bullets[0]", "snippet": "Migrated 200 nightly Hive jobs to Spark on Kubernetes, halving warehouse spend"}}]}
